beats.subline: Wednesday, September 2, 2026 close — a broad rebound snapped a two-day losing streak as bond yields eased and the Fed's Williams downplayed a September hike.
beats.body: Stocks bounced back from Tuesday's Iran-driven slide as long-dated Treasury yields eased and the dollar weakened; New York Fed President John Williams said there are 'no clear signs right now' that a September rate hike is needed, tempering the inflation worries that had weighed on sentiment.

beats.headline: Trump privately weighs declaring the Iran war over even as Pentagon extends troop deployments
beats.body: The Wall Street Journal reports Trump has told aides he favors declaring an end to the seven-month conflict, betting that economic pressure will eventually force Tehran to dismantle its nuclear program or collapse, while Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is simultaneously extending deployment timelines for the roughly 50,000 US troops, 19 warships and two carrier strike groups in the region into 2027, a sign the Pentagon is hedging against the fighting continuing.

beats.headline: Taiwan pairs drones with artillery for faster targeting as analysts warn of PLA precision-strike risk
beats.body: Taiwan's Third, Fourth and Fifth Operational Zones ran live-fire drills integrating unmanned systems into artillery targeting, letting drones spot targets and feed coordinates straight to firing units for a faster kill chain; the joint ISW-AEI China & Taiwan Update cautioned that Taiwan's high-end artillery could still be vulnerable to PLA precision strikes in a real conflict, drawing on lessons from how drone-corrected fire has stalled large mechanized offensives in Ukraine.
beats.source: AEI / Institute for the Study of War

beats.headline: US forces hit Iranian coastal defenses in sixth straight night of strikes as Hormuz standoff continues
beats.body: CENTCOM said fighter jets, drones and warships struck dozens of Iranian targets — coastal surveillance sites, air defenses, logistics hubs and maritime assets — in the sixth consecutive night of strikes aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, even as the White House privately debates whether to declare the broader war over.

beats.headline: Army awards AeroVironment its first-ever production contract for laser weapons
beats.body: AeroVironment won a $464.8 million Army Other Transaction Agreement for dozens of 30-kilowatt LOCUST X3 laser systems, mountable on the JLTV and other platforms to shoot down small drones, marking the first-ever US production award for a directed-energy weapon and a shift from prototype to fielded capability for the Army's layered air defense.

beats.headline: OpenAI clears its Astra model for release after it became the first AI to cross a 'Critical' cyber-risk threshold
beats.body: Astra can independently find and exploit unpatched software vulnerabilities without step-by-step human direction, the first model to hit OpenAI's 'Critical' rating under its Preparedness Framework; OpenAI says new safeguards sufficiently manage the risk, so a small group of testers will get initial access with broader release gated behind its Daybreak Blue cybersecurity program, alongside similarly restricted-access cyber models Anthropic and Google rolled out the same week.

beats.headline: Cornerbacks Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson back as full practice participants ahead of opener
beats.body: Both starting corners, who'd been day-to-day after picking up injuries in joint practice with the Titans, looked like full participants in Wednesday's practice and are trending toward availability for the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina, while running back Kyle Monangai remains week-to-week on a knee injury that initial tests showed was structurally sound.
